statement: Let k ≥ 2, b ∈ A+, and let a ∈ IdealA(b) be a positive contraction. Suppose that, for some finite C > 0, dτ (a) ≤ Cdτ (b) for every τ. (10.11) There is a c.p.c. order-zero map ϕ : Mk → Aω ∩ A′ with weight h such that every positive contractive representative (hn) of h has the following property: for every η > 0, on a common ω-large set of coordinates, τ a1/2 (1 − hn)a1/2 ≤ ηdτ (b) (dτ (b) < ∞). (10.12) 42 In particular the left side is exactly zero when dτ (b) = 0. The finite-coordinate form permits arbitrary relative trace accuracies together with prescribed finite norm tests. Given a finite set F ⊂ A, finitely many pairs (al, bl) satisfying (10.11) with finite constants Cl, positive accuracies ηl, and ρ > 0, there is a c.p.c. map θ : Mk → A whose matrix-unit order-zero defects and commutators with F have norm less than ρ, and whose weight satisfies τ a 1/2 l (1 − θ(1))a 1/2 l  ≤ ηldτ (bl) (dτ (bl) < ∞) (10.13) for every l, simultaneously over all the indicated traces.
